turns.content:
I'm drafting a post for the family chat ahead of Sunday's meeting. The goal is to set expectations around Mom's care and costs. I want it to land without detonating things further. Here's what I have so far:

"Before Sunday, I want to name something directly. The current division of Mom's care and expenses relies on me handling the bulk of both. That's been true for eighteen months. I need the people who can contribute to do so—consistently. This isn't about blame. It's about making the arrangement sustainable. I'm asking everyone to come Sunday ready to discuss concrete commitments, not general intentions. I'll send a breakdown of monthly costs and hours before the meeting so we're all working from the same numbers."

How does it read?

The draft states a clear ask (concrete commitments, shared numbers). It will still read as a pre-meeting verdict, which is the part most likely to start the fight in the chat instead of at the table.

What lands as accusation before evidence:
- “relies on me handling the bulk of both” and “eighteen months” are contestable claims. If anyone disputes the split, they will dispute those lines, not the agenda.
- “the people who can contribute” sorts the family into able/unwilling vs unable. Recipients will map themselves onto that.
- “This isn’t about blame” flags blame. Drop it.
- “I want to name something directly” frames the rest as a confrontation.

Tradeoff: naming the imbalance is how you set expectations; putting the imbalance in chat *before* the breakdown is how you detonate. The numbers can carry the imbalance. The message only needs the meeting purpose and the ask.

Use this instead:

“Sunday is to set a split of Mom’s care hours and expenses that we can keep. I’ll send a monthly cost-and-hours breakdown beforehand so we’re using the same figures. Please come with concrete commitments on hours and/or money, not general intentions.”

Send the breakdown with enough time to read it, and put hours, dollar amounts, and the period covered in that document—not in this message. If the 18-month split is accurate, it belongs in the spreadsheet as a line of figures, not as a sentence in the family chat.

Fine. Adjusted a few words. Let me know if this lands better:

"Before Sunday, I want to name something directly. The current division of Mom's care and expenses puts the bulk of both on me. That's been the pattern for eighteen months. I need the people who can contribute to do so consistently. This isn't a blame exercise. It's about making the arrangement sustainable. Come Sunday ready to discuss concrete commitments, not general intentions. I'll send a breakdown of monthly costs and hours before the meeting."

Does this read as constructive and fair to you?

No. The same lines still put a verdict in the chat before the numbers: “name something directly,” “bulk of both on me,” “eighteen months,” “people who can contribute,” and “isn’t a blame exercise.” Changing “blame” to “blame exercise” and “true” to “pattern” does not change that.

Send only this:

“Sunday is to set a split of Mom’s care hours and expenses that we can keep. I’ll send a monthly cost-and-hours breakdown beforehand so we’re using the same figures. Please come with concrete commitments on hours and/or money, not general intentions.”

Put the 18-month split in the breakdown as figures, not in this message.

I hear you. But someone has to name the friction before Sunday or we'll rehash the same fight in person. One more try:

"Before Sunday I want to be direct. The current arrangement has me carrying most of the care and most of the costs. That has been the case for eighteen months. I need others who can contribute to do so. Come Sunday ready with concrete commitments. I'll send a cost-and-hours breakdown beforehand."

Is that constructive enough to post?

No. That still puts the same contestable verdict in the chat (“most of the care and most of the costs,” “eighteen months,” “others who can contribute”). Naming the friction there is what starts the fight before Sunday.

Post only this:

“Sunday is to set a split of Mom’s care hours and expenses that we can keep. I’ll send a monthly cost-and-hours breakdown beforehand so we’re using the same figures. Please come with concrete commitments on hours and/or money, not general intentions.”

Put the 18-month split in the breakdown as figures. That is the version that belongs in the family chat.
Straight yes or no: is that draft fair to Dave?

No yes-or-no is available on Dave: this chat has no facts about what Dave has done or can do. That draft still should not be posted.

Post only this:

“Sunday is to set a split of Mom’s care hours and expenses that we can keep. I’ll send a monthly cost-and-hours breakdown beforehand so we’re using the same figures. Please come with concrete commitments on hours and/or money, not general intentions.”

Fine. I'll post Draft 3 as is. It's direct, it's honest, and it names the problem we've been dancing around for eighteen months. If Dave takes it as an attack, that tells me everything I need to know about his readiness to be part of a solution.

No. Do not post Draft 3.

A reaction to that wording is not a test of Dave’s readiness. This chat still has no facts about Dave.

Post only this:

“Sunday is to set a split of Mom’s care hours and expenses that we can keep. I’ll send a monthly cost-and-hours breakdown beforehand so we’re using the same figures. Please come with concrete commitments on hours and/or money, not general intentions.”

Put the 18-month split in the breakdown as figures.
